corpus_integrity.claim: The held-out set was rerun unchanged, as required for comparability with the stated bar.
corpus_integrity.method: Regenerated from the fixed seed and diffed against the recorded run phase3_bench_heldout_20260926-143632.json.
corpus_integrity.conclusion: Identical corpus. The new number is directly comparable to the 75% bar.

resolved_model.requirement: Log the actually-resolved model before running anything.
resolved_model.note: engine.cloud_available reports False, which is a REPORTING BUG: ai_engine.py:194 derives it from OpenRouterProvider only, and OpenRouter has no key here. It must not be read as Groq being unavailable.

backend_ordering.status: UNCHANGED - still chosen on measured id-validity, not latency
backend_ordering.note: The earlier iteration had reordered to auto-first purely on measured latency (auto mean 2.89s vs cloud 9.86s) and was reverted because auto/cloud invented non-existent ids. That revert is intact.

timeout.status: UNCHANGED - the bounded hybrid, which is NEITHER of the two reverted extremes
timeout.detail: Blocking on success (shutdown(wait=True)); non-blocking on timeout/error (shutdown(wait=False)) with a bounded in-flight cap of _MAX_INFLIGHT_CALLS=6.
timeout.unbounded_non_blocking_would_be: shutdown(wait=False) with no cap - this is the change that collapsed accuracy 7/10 -> 2/10 and it is NOT present
timeout.pure_blocking_would_be: context-managed executor, which defeats its own timeout (measured 51.9s against an 8s budget)
timeout.new_this_rerun: Added GENESIS_LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT / GENESIS_LLM_TOTAL_BUDGET environment overrides so a batch measurement can raise budgets without changing interactive production defaults. Production defaults are unchanged when the variables are unset.

headline_result.why: 27 of the 40 items never reached the model. The provider's rolling tokens-per-minute quota was exhausted partway through the run, and LLMIntentResolver.resolve() catches ProviderError internally and returns None, so an exhausted quota is indistinguishable from 'the model declined' by the time it reaches the scorer. Those 27 items all returned in under 1 second, which no real model call can do.
headline_result.harness_defect_found_and_fixed: The first cloud run reported quota_errors=0 because it only counted exceptions that escaped decide(), and decide() never raises. The scorer now flags sub-second no-answers as suspected quota starvation and reports a separate measured-subset rate.

caveats: Sample is 13 of 40 and is not a substitute for a full run.
Two of the 13 'answered' items completed in 0.0s, which means the deterministic layer answered them, not the LLM.
Four of the 13 took 22-85s, i.e. they hit the raised budget rather than answering cleanly.
69.2% is below the 75% bar, but it is not a defensible pass or fail on its own.

root_cause_of_the_429.finding: It is a rolling tokens-per-minute quota, not a size ceiling and not a hard block.
root_cause_of_the_429.evidence: A short prompt ('Reply with only the word: ok') succeeded while the 5480-token enriched catalog 429'd. After waiting, prompts of 6794, 8794, 10794, 12794, 15794, 18794, 21794 and 26694 chars ALL succeeded, including the exact size that had just been failing.
root_cause_of_the_429.consequence_for_the_benchmark: 40 items x 5480 tokens = ~219,000 tokens. The quota tolerates roughly 3 full-size requests per window, so an unpaced or lightly paced batch drains it and measures rate limiting instead of routing.

prompt_budget_measured.conclusion: Even the cheapest catalog form needs ~127k tokens for 40 items. Prompt trimming alone cannot make a 40-item cloud run fit the observed quota.

substantive_finding_this_rerun.name: looks_actionable imposed a hard ceiling that no model could clear
substantive_finding_this_rerun.significance: Before the fix, 65% of the corpus could not reach ANY model, so the maximum achievable score on this corpus was 35% - below the 75% bar regardless of model quality. The bar was unreachable for a reason that had nothing to do with the model.
rejection_causes_observed: typo in the verb: 'please reda current screen brightness' (reda/read), 'please insepct' , 'please exeucte', 'please deltee'
non-English politeness the stripper did not know: "s'il vous plait, permanently empty the Recycle Bin"
unstripped lead-in frame: 'when you get a chance, copy text to the system clipboard'
ordinary verbs absent from the whitelist: execute, report, download, evaluate, skip, inspect
substantive_finding_this_rerun.fix: The gate is now evidence-based rather than positional. It passes a request when there is computer-DOMAIN evidence (an explicit technical noun, or any word drawn from the live capability registry's own vocabulary) or an unambiguous non-generic action verb, and it rejects narration and small talk. Domain vocabulary is derived from the registry, so a new capability's own words become evidence for it automatically instead of requiring anyone to maintain a noun list.
regressions_caught_and_fixed_during_the_: Generic verbs leaked conversation through: 'you make me happy' and 'i think we should set up a meeting' both passed because make/set are in the verb list. Fixed by splitting generic verbs out of the standalone-evidence set.
An unpaired state hint leaked a greeting: 'hi how are you doing today' passed on 'doing'. Fixed by restoring the original rule that a state hint only counts alongside domain evidence.

Fuzzy vocabulary matching produced only false positives ('control my computer' matched the vocab entries 'controls' and 'compute' at ratio 0.93) while adding nothing, because every real held-out item already matched an exact vocabulary word. Removed; typo tolerance now applies only to the action-verb check where a misspelling is unambiguous.
substantive_finding_this_rerun.pinned_behaviour_preserved: All previously pinned gate cases still hold: the 5 actionable samples pass, and 'what is the capital of france', 'hello there friend', 'you make me happy', 'i think we should set up a meeting', 'hii now i make you able to control my computer' and 'she set the table before we arrived' are all still blocked.

routing_precedence_bug.status: STILL PRESENT, and it is a larger problem than the model-capacity issue it was previously blamed on
routing_precedence_bug.previously_reported: The LLM correctly selected media.play_pause for 'what is playing right now' but the request ended at Level 1.
routing_precedence_bug.this_rerun: With a 120B model reachable, 31 of 40 items still produced no Level 3 decision. Tracing showed the gate was the dominant cause (65% blocked), which is now fixed. The residual cause is the guard at workflow_decision.py:1609 (_is_conversational_or_educational) plus deterministic answers outranking correct LLM answers; both remain unfixed.
routing_precedence_bug.why_not_fixed_here: Each changes routing precedence for phrasing that currently works. Doing so without a valid accuracy measurement would trade a known number for an unknown one.

verdict.bar_unchanged: 75% - deliberately NOT adjusted to fit the observed number
verdict.on_the_bar_itself: The bar is still defensible in principle, but this rerun exposed that it was partly unreachable for a reason unrelated to model quality: the 65% gate ceiling capped the corpus at 35% before any model was consulted. That ceiling is now removed. The bar should be re-evaluated only once a valid full-corpus measurement is possible, and it should be re-evaluated against a corpus with realistic user phrasing rather than registry-descriptor boilerplate.
verdict.primary_blocker: The enriched catalog prompt (~5.4k tokens) exceeds the Groq account's rolling tokens-per-minute quota, so the capable model cannot be measured on a 40-item corpus. This is an infrastructure limit, not a capability limit.
verdict.secondary_blocker: The conversational guard and deterministic-over-LLM precedence still discard correct semantic answers.
what_would_close_it: Cloud access with a token quota that can serve ~219k tokens for a 40-item run, or a measured 10-20 item subset with the same rigor.
A locally installed model of >=7B, which removes the quota dependency entirely (the only local model today is qwen2.5:0.5b, 397,821,319 parameters).
Fix the residual routing-precedence guards now that the gate ceiling is gone.
Shrink the catalog via a two-stage shortlist-then-detail call, which would cut tokens per request enough to fit a much smaller quota and would also fix the 30-40s interactive latency.
